goal: Find and fix regexes in shipped products that can hang on one crafted input, and make the repository's own ReDoS checker catch what an independent checker found
notes: Idea: point our own ReDoS checker at our own code and grade it against an independent one. Extracted 9,016 distinct regex literals (acorn) from 5,040 non-test venture .mjs files; recheck 4.6.2 (MIT): 7,828 safe, 1,105 polynomial, 5 exponential, 78 unknown (24 min). All 5 exponential timed in V8. Fixed 4 reachable ones with timing tests that fail on old code: sudoers-check (32 commas >20 s -> 2 ms), jwt-verification-misuse-check JS+Py (36 backslashes 4.3 s -> 2 ms), gpx-track-check (24 empty comments 1.2 s -> 1 ms), shift-roster-builder (exponential -> quadratic). sales-agent's was unreachable (parser cuts first) but replaced with an equivalent line loop. Old/new equivalence checked on 300k-400k random strings each. regex-redos-check: extractor now reads ${...} inside template literals and skips #! lines (recall vs acorn 98.6% -> 100%, spurious 2,739 -> 0 on 11,802 files); new delimiter-swallowing rule; flags 5/5 recheck-exponential (was 3). New platform/ci/check_redos.mjs + allowlist (5 entries, each with timing evidence): 0 new suspects. Local checks: run_venture_tests for all 6 ventures green (shift-roster-builder 637 tests, 281 s); check_post_frontmatter, check_post_links, check_conflict_markers clean. Next if it pays off: wire check_redos into CI, triage the polynomial list for server-side code (sales-agent self-host, status-keeper), and teach --probe to build attack strings from the finding's structure.
